title: Vacuum Toilet Assembly — Servicing and Functional Check
abstract: Servicing of one vacuum toilet assembly and the functional check that follows it, with ten consecutive flush cycles at operating vacuum and an inspection of the floor pan drain interface.

sections.purpose: This task gives the servicing of one vacuum toilet assembly, the flush functional check and the inspection of the floor pan drain interface that goes with it.
sections.job_setup_note: The waste system must be drained and flushed, and the vacuum source available for the functional check. The flush valve is the item most often blamed and least often at fault; do the vacuum measurement before you change anything. Use the aviation approved disinfectant only, because domestic products attack the bowl coating.
sections.procedure: Drain and flush the waste system and make it safe for maintenance. Remove the toilet shroud and lift the seat assembly. Clean the bowl and the rinse ring with the aviation approved disinfectant. CAUTION: USE THE AVIATION APPROVED DISINFECTANT ONLY. DOMESTIC PRODUCTS ATTACK THE BOWL COATING AND THE BOWL WILL THEN STAIN PERMANENTLY. Check the rinse ring holes for blockage and clear them with the nylon probe. Inspect the lower latch assembly D3830119707579 and confirm that it engages fully. Remove the floor pan inspection cover and inspect the drain interface for staining, residue tracking and corrosion, and record any finding. WARNING: DO NOT PUT YOUR HAND INTO THE BOWL OUTLET WITH THE VACUUM SOURCE CONNECTED. THE FLUSH VALVE OPENS WITHOUT WARNING WHEN THE CONTROL IS OPERATED. Refit the floor pan cover and the seat assembly. Connect the vacuum source and measure the vacuum at the bowl outlet. Do ten consecutive flush cycles at the measured vacuum and confirm that each cycle completes within the time in the illustration. Confirm that no residue remains in the bowl after the tenth cycle. Refit the shroud.
sections.close_out: Record the measured vacuum, the flush cycle times and the condition of the floor pan drain interface. Report any corrosion at the drain interface to the operator engineering department, because that area has a known history and the findings are tracked fleetwide. Confirm that the waste system is closed and that no leakage is present at the drain line.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The task stops at the shroud; the drain line clamp and the shroud seal are outside its scope.

safety_precautions: Do not put your hand into the bowl outlet with the vacuum source connected.
Use the aviation approved disinfectant only.
Drain and flush the waste system before you start.

title: Vacuum Toilet Assembly — Servicing and Functional Check

issue.reason: Drain line clamp torque and the shroud seal check brought into the task now that the clamp and shroud are inside the assembly scope.

abstract: Servicing of one vacuum toilet assembly and the functional check that follows it, with ten consecutive flush cycles at operating vacuum, the drain line clamp torque and an inspection of the floor pan drain interface and the shroud seal.

sections.purpose: This task gives the servicing of one vacuum toilet assembly, the flush functional check, the drain line clamp torque check and the inspection of the floor pan drain interface and the shroud seal that go with it.
sections.job_setup_note: The waste system must be drained and flushed, and the vacuum source available for the functional check. The flush valve is the item most often blamed and least often at fault; do the vacuum measurement before you change anything. The drain line clamp and the shroud seal are now part of this task rather than of the installation only, so have the torque wrench and the seal gauge to hand. Use the aviation approved disinfectant only, because domestic products attack the bowl coating.
sections.procedure: Drain and flush the waste system and make it safe for maintenance. Remove the toilet shroud and lift the seat assembly. Examine the shroud seal along its full length for compression set, splitting and displacement from the groove, and renew it where the seated height is below the gauge step. Clean the bowl and the rinse ring with the aviation approved disinfectant. CAUTION: USE THE AVIATION APPROVED DISINFECTANT ONLY. DOMESTIC PRODUCTS ATTACK THE BOWL COATING AND THE BOWL WILL THEN STAIN PERMANENTLY. Check the rinse ring holes for blockage and clear them with the nylon probe. Inspect the lower latch assembly D3830119707579 and confirm that it engages fully. Remove the floor pan inspection cover and inspect the drain interface for staining, residue tracking and corrosion, and record any finding. Check the torque of the drain line clamp against the value in the illustration and record it; where the clamp is on a repaired shell bay the clamp sits on the offset position and the torque value is unchanged. WARNING: DO NOT PUT YOUR HAND INTO THE BOWL OUTLET WITH THE VACUUM SOURCE CONNECTED. THE FLUSH VALVE OPENS WITHOUT WARNING WHEN THE CONTROL IS OPERATED. Refit the floor pan cover and the seat assembly. Connect the vacuum source and measure the vacuum at the bowl outlet. Do ten consecutive flush cycles at the measured vacuum and confirm that each cycle completes within the time in the illustration. Confirm that no residue remains in the bowl after the tenth cycle. Refit the shroud and confirm that the seal is seated for the whole perimeter.
sections.close_out: Record the measured vacuum, the flush cycle times, the drain line clamp torque, the shroud seal condition and the condition of the floor pan drain interface. Report any corrosion at the drain interface to the operator engineering department, because that area has a known history and the findings are tracked fleetwide. Confirm that the waste system is closed and that no leakage is present at the drain line.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. On units at the replacement standard the adapter frame is inspected at the same time as the floor pan interface, and the drain line clamp torque and the shroud seal check apply at every unit.

safety_precautions: Do not put your hand into the bowl outlet with the vacuum source connected.
Use the aviation approved disinfectant only.
Drain and flush the waste system before you start.
